description: We are a driven team passionate about machine learning, competitive problem-solving, and space technology, focused on turning complex data into complete, high-impact hackathon solutions. With strong technical expertise in Python, PyTorch, and AI data pipelines, we bring solid engineering and fast execution to the table to build ambitious, working prototypes before the deadline.
summary:
Earth never stands still, but most surface change is invisible to the people who need to see it. Project SBTX is an interactive web app that makes it visible. Pick any place on Earth and any two dates, a before/after slider shows exactly what changed. Switch between image types to reveal different aspects of the surface. Ask Gemini to explain the change in plain language.

The app is built on radar remote sensing, which sees through cloud, smoke and darkness. That makes it useful for wildfires, floods, glacier retreat, wetland loss and farming activity, wherever and whenever they happen. A Python and PyTorch pipeline turns raw radar data into clear visuals. Gemini explains what the user sees, and the imagery stays the evidence.
details:
The problem

Surface change is constant and global, but radar data is technical. Researchers, responders, farmers and students often can’t read it. Optical imagery fails under cloud, smoke and night, which are the conditions where fires and floods happen.

What we built

  • Location and time picker: Choose anywhere on Earth and any two dates.
  • Before/after slider: Compare two terrestrial areas or two moments side by side.
  • Image type selection: View the same place in different radar-derived renderings.
  • Gemini analysis: One click gives a plain-language description of the visible change and its likely causes.

How it works

  1. Radar imagery is ingested for the chosen place and dates.
  2. A Python pipeline processes and aligns the scenes.
  3. A step highlights change between the two dates.
  4. The web interface renders the results with the slider and image-type options.
  5. Gemini receives the selected context and returns an explanation.

How space agency data was used

The challenge centers on NISAR radar data extracted from NASA's Earthdata (https://search.asf.alaska.edu/#/). We used these to train our models.

Tools and technology

Python, a custom AI data pipeline, a web front end, and the Gemini API.

Impact

  • Disaster response: faster damage mapping when clouds or smoke block optical satellites.
  • Agriculture: tracking land use and farming activity.
  • Research: exploring surface change without heavy tooling.
  • Education: teaching with real satellite data.

Limitations

  • Gemini’s explanations are interpretive and can be wrong. They support the imagery and don’t replace it.
  • Accuracy depends on data availability and the roughly 12-day NISAR revisit cycle.
  • Change detection shows where the surface changed. It doesn’t prove why.

Next steps

  • Time-lapse mode across many dates
  • Automatic alerts for changes in watched areas
  • Automated change classification (fire, flood, ice, vegetation)
